transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-14
Start time (UTC): 15:00
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Chan (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SRE), Priya Kapoor (Halcyon NetOps), Darren Miles (Halcyon Platform Eng), Sophie Li (Halcyon Security), Tom Garcia (Halcyon ML Infra)
Recording id: poc-20270514-halcyon-8342

Summary: quick readout of last week's netops tests, quantization profile results, KMS/SOC2 follow-ups, and next steps for a head-to-head latency comparison. Discussed a small regression on p99 for longer context due to quant kernel selection; agreed to run a controlled 1k request profile and a rollback drill if needed.

Topics: netops handshake, routing fallbacks, quantization impact, kernel compatibility, KMS integration, audit logs/retention, upcoming benchmark runs

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: All right team, thanks for joining — um — let's do a quick roll call. Marcus, Ravi, you there?
[00:06] Marcus Chan: Yep here. Doing fine.
[00:07] Ravi Patel: Yep.
[00:09] Priya Kapoor: Priya on the line. Apologies for being a few minutes late, bandwidth spike earlier.
[00:13] Darren Miles: Darren here.
[00:14] Sophie Li: Sophie.
[00:15] Tom Garcia: Tom.
[00:17] Lena Ortiz: Cool. Agenda for 50 minutes — Marcus will walk the quant profile, then we'll cover the netops handshake failures we saw yesterday, KMS / SOC questions from Sophie, and then decide a follow-up plan. If we get through early we can do a quick kernel rollback simulation.

[02:05] Marcus Chan: Okay so quick context: we ran the quantized model build on the private pilot cluster in Halcyon's VPC. The short version: top-line token throughput improved 18% on average, cost per token reduced, but we did see p99 latency regressions for sequences over 1.2k tokens. I think that's a kernel selection edge-case where the runtime picks the mixed-int path and the kv cache replay hits a slower code path — or at least that's my hypothesis.
[02:40] Tom Garcia: When you say p99 regressed, are we talking 100–200 ms or multi-second?
[02:44] Marcus Chan: In our tests p50 stayed ~unchanged, p95 was modestly better, but p99 increased ~430 ms on average for sequences >1.2k. There were some outliers ~1.8–2.3s but those correlated with specific GPU context switches during neighbor jobs.
[03:10] Priya Kapoor: We also saw some dropped keepalives on the private egress path yesterday during the kernel rollout, not sure if that's related.
[03:18] Ravi Patel: The keepalive drops match the egress ACL churn window — we pushed a route update and the connection NAT mapping cycled. I have log snippets — I'll attach.
[03:27] Darren Miles: Right, we did a small BGP flapping test to validate failovers and we might have triggered a NAT timeout. We didn't expect keepalives to be that brittle.

[04:10] Marcus Chan: Notes on the quant profile itself: we ran 3 workloads — short chat (<=256 tokens), mid (256-1.2k), and long (>1.2k). Short and mid showed 12–22% CPU and throughput wins; long sequences hit the slower kernel path. I've got a spreadsheet link with raw traces and the kernel selection map. (link: https://redwood.co/shared/poc-halcyon/quant-profile-20270514)
[04:44] Tom Garcia: Can you share which kernel versions? We need to map to our internal patch matrix.
[04:48] Marcus Chan: Sure — builds v2.9.3-quant1 (Redwood runtime), with a fallback kernel 2.9.2-standard. The quant path uses the new fused-attn kernel; fallback uses the older NV fused implementation.
[05:05] Sophie Li: Quick security question: with quantization we still need to ensure keys never leave the HSM. How's KMS integrated for private?
[05:15] Lena Ortiz: Good call — we use a customer-managed KMS with an envelope encryption pattern. Redwood stores only wrapped keys and never persists plaintext. We'll send our KMS integration diagram. Marcus, I'll attach the SOC2 excerpt Sophie asked for.
[05:34] Sophie Li: Thanks. Also audit logs: retention policies — do you store telemetry in the cloud? We need to ensure logs for inference requests are kept for 13 months for our compliance program.
[05:47] Marcus Chan: Telemetry by default streams to the Redwood control plane with 90-day retention. For Private we can configure a log sink to their Splunk or S3 with custom retention. That pattern will preserve logs and meet 13 months.
[06:05] Priya Kapoor: Ok that helps. On networking: yesterday's netops test showed three brief failovers where traffic shifted to the secondary egress and we observed increased tail latency. We have PCAPs and traceroutes.
[06:20] Ravi Patel: I reviewed the PCAPs. The failovers correlate to our route-change timer not honoring the keepalive window; some TCP sessions reestablished and that bumped the initial handshake path. For short-lived inference bursts that causes retries and spikes.
[06:35] Darren Miles: So recommendation — can Redwood add sticky routing for sessions or an intermediate connection pool to smooth the handoff?
[06:41] Marcus Chan: We have a connection pooling knob in the runtime — affinity TTL. We can increase the session affinity to 45s for the pilot and that should reduce reconnections during BGP churn. There's a config patch — I'll propose values in the ticket.
[07:00] Priya Kapoor: Would increasing affinity hurt scaling? If affinity keeps sessions long, can we saturate a few GPUs?
[07:06] Marcus Chan: Good point. For Halcyon traffic shapes we think 45s will be safe; throughput tests showed no saturation at that TTL. We'll run a synthetic with the affinity change to prove it.

[08:30] Tom Garcia: Back to quant — is it possible to preferentially route long-context requests to the standard (non-quant) model variant while short requests use the quant model? That would give best of both worlds.
[08:40] Lena Ortiz: Yes, smart routing is supported. We can add a policy in the routing table: if sequence_length > 1.2k then route to model: rwdl-2.9.2-standard; else route to rwdl-2.9.3-quant1. That can be live patched.
[08:58] Sophie Li: Will that policy cause additional egress for model switching? I worry about audit and egress costs.
[09:04] Marcus Chan: It’s just an internal route rule; no extra egress beyond the normal inference traffic. We do surface routing events in the audit log though so you'll be able to track policy decisions.

[10:20] Lena Ortiz: Action item — Marcus to run the 1k request quant profile and include kernel-level traces. Also Marcus to spin the affinity TTL test. Marcus, can you confirm both by EOD Monday?
[10:32] Marcus Chan: Yep, I'll kick it off tomorrow and share the sheet by 2027-05-18.
[10:36] Priya Kapoor: On the netops side we'll coordinate BGP flapping window and see if we can produce a synthetic that fails over predictably; we'll share trace times.
[10:45] Darren Miles: We'll also run the hosted vs dedicated latency test as requested — baseline against your hosted endpoints and the private VPC endpoints. Preference is to run during our low traffic window Tuesday morning.
[11:00] Sophie Li: For SOC / KMS stuff, can Redwood provide the KMS handshake flow diagram and a sample wrapped key header? We can't store wrapped keys locally without a diagram to sign off.
[11:12] Lena Ortiz: Absolutely. I'll push the KMS diagram and SOC2 excerpt. Marcus, add the wrapped-key sample to the shared secure folder.

[12:40] Tom Garcia: A couple of nitty bits from ML infra: memory pinning on our side interacts poorly with the fused kernels — sometimes we see transient OOM signals during warmup. Any mitigations?
[12:52] Marcus Chan: We introduced a staggered warmup and reduced prefetch concurrency in the quant path. It helped in our lab but we need to validate in Halcyon's workload. I'll add those flags to the test matrix.
[13:10] Priya Kapoor: Also we noticed the telemetry tag names differ between our tracing and Redwood's default labels; mapping would help for our observability.
[13:18] Ravi Patel: We can push a mapping layer — Marcus, can you share the telemetry schema?
[13:22] Marcus Chan: Yes, schema link: (link: https://redwood.co/shared/poc-halcyon/telemetry-schema-20270514)

[14:50] Darren Miles: Competitors question — we ran a quick eval of Vertex AI earlier this month and saw similar quant benefits but the control plane didn't expose kernel-level traces which made debugging harder. Redwood's traces are helpful.
[15:03] Lena Ortiz: That's good to hear. We do try to make the runtime signals available for pilots.

[16:20] Marcus Chan: Quick note on the GPU context switches — we saw correlation with concurrent batch jobs in the same compute pool. For the pilot we recommend isolating pilot workloads to a dedicated node pool or enforcing soft quotas so that context switches are minimized.
[16:36] Tom Garcia: We can do a dedicated node pool for the pilot. We'll schedule that for the Tuesday runs.

[18:00] Priya Kapoor: KMS question again — how do you rotate wrapped keys for long-running sessions? If a key rotates mid-session will the session fail?
[18:12] Marcus Chan: We have a rolling unwrap mechanism and a short grace period for active sessions. For private deployment with HSM-backed KMS, rotation is seamless as long as the wrapped key header version is recognized. We'll include the exact header schema in the doc.

[20:05] Sophie Li: I still need the retention SLA for audit logs formalized. Email would be fine.
[20:11] Lena Ortiz: We'll send that today; consider it done.

[21:40] Marcus Chan: Proposed experiments (summary): 1) affinity TTL bump to 45s and run load test; 2) quant 1k-run with kernel tracing; 3) long-context routing policy to send >1.2k to non-quant model; 4) warmup concurrency reduction test. I'll attach flags and expected metrics.
[22:02] Tom Garcia: Sounds good. Also add memory pressure test during warmup.
[22:10] Marcus Chan: Noted.

[24:30] Lena Ortiz: Let's set a concrete timeline — run affinity + warmup tests Monday, quant profile Wednesday (Marcus), hosted vs dedicated latency runs Tuesday morning (Darren), docs and KMS by next Thursday. We should reconvene the following Thursday at the same time. Does that work?
[24:52] Darren Miles: Works for us.
[25:00] Priya Kapoor: Works.

[26:30] Sophie Li: One last ask — if quant introduces an accuracy regression for specific prompts, how will Redwood surface that? We need alerts not just performance signals.
[26:42] Marcus Chan: We can attach a regression hook to your eval set; Redwood Optimize can run a quick eval on each build and post a quality delta. If the quality delta crosses a threshold we'll trigger a rollback or route shift. We'll include the eval config in the artifact bundle.
[27:00] Sophie Li: Great.

[28:10] Lena Ortiz: Ok quick recap of decisions and owners — Marcus runs the quant and affinity TTL experiments and shares artifacts; Lena sends KMS and SOC2 doc; Halcyon runs hosted vs dedicated latency runs and shares PCAPs/traces; Sophie to confirm retention requirement doc. We'll meet next Thursday same time.

[29:05] Marcus Chan: I'll also open a ticket for the kernel fallback observation so the runtime team can look at kernel heuristics.

[29:40] Priya Kapoor: We'll schedule our BGP failover window for Tuesday 02:00 UTC to coincide with Darren's latency tests.

[30:00] Lena Ortiz: Great. Any other questions?
[30:06] Tom Garcia: None from me.
[30:08] Sophie Li: No.
[30:09] Darren Miles: Good. Thanks.
[30:10] Lena Ortiz: Thanks everyone. We'll close and send the notes.

[30:20] Recording end (approx).

Notes / artifacts referenced: shared spreadsheet with quant traces (https://redwood.co/shared/poc-halcyon/quant-profile-20270514), telemetry schema (https://redwood.co/shared/poc-halcyon/telemetry-schema-20270514), tentative KMS diagram (to be sent), SOC2 excerpt (to be sent).

Caveats: transcription may contain mis-attributed phrases (e.g., "kv cache" as "K V cash") and timestamps are approximate.
